```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(officer.pptx)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

shape_example_pptx <- function() {
  source_candidates <- c(
    file.path("inst/ext/pptx/shapes.pptx"),
    file.path("..", "inst/ext/pptx/shapes.pptx"),
    system.file("ext/pptx/shapes.pptx", package = "officer.pptx")
  )
  source_path <- source_candidates[file.exists(source_candidates)][1]
  if (is.na(source_path)) {
    stop("Example file not found: shapes.pptx", call. = FALSE)
  }
  source_path
}

shape_thumbnail <- function(name) {
  vapply(name, function(one_name) {
    source_candidates <- c(
      file.path("inst/ext/vignettes/shape-select-thumbnails", one_name),
      file.path("..", "inst/ext/vignettes/shape-select-thumbnails", one_name),
      system.file(
        "ext/vignettes/shape-select-thumbnails",
        one_name,
        package = "officer.pptx"
      )
    )
    source_path <- source_candidates[file.exists(source_candidates)][1]
    if (is.na(source_path)) {
      stop("Thumbnail not found: ", one_name, call. = FALSE)
    }
    local_dir <- "shape-select-thumbnails"
    dir.create(local_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
    local_path <- file.path(local_dir, one_name)
    file.copy(source_path, local_path, overwrite = TRUE)
    local_path
  }, character(1))
}
```

## Why Select Shapes?

Use the `shape_*()` functions when a PowerPoint template already contains objects that should be found and edited from R. This is useful for template-driven workflows where designers place marker shapes such as `{tag_1}` or `{tag_2}` on slides, and R later fills or updates those markers.

The basic workflow is:

1. Place a visible marker in a PowerPoint shape or text box.
2. Find the marker with `shape_select()`.
3. Inspect the result if needed.
4. Update the selected shape with `shape_update()`.

The `shape_*()` functions are experimental. Their core use case is stable enough for template workflows, but argument names, supported shape kinds, and edge-case behavior may still change while the API is refined.

The examples below use the packaged PowerPoint file `shapes.pptx`. It contains one slide with three marker shapes.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(shape_thumbnail("thumb-shape-marker.png"))
```

```{r}
x <- read_pptx(shape_example_pptx())

shape_select(x)[, c("slide_idx", "name", "text", "left", "top", "width", "height")]
```

## A Typical Update

In practice, you usually select a marker and immediately update it. The selection can be piped directly into `shape_update()`, which returns the modified presentation.

```{r}
x <- x |>
  shape_select(text = "{tag_1}", match = "exact") |>
  shape_update(
    text = "Image placeholder",
    background = "#E6F4EA",
    line = sp_line(color = "#408335", lwd = 1.5),
    name = "Image placeholder marker"
  )

shape_select(x, name = "Image placeholder marker", match = "exact")[
  , c("slide_idx", "name", "text", "left", "top", "width", "height")
]
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(shape_thumbnail("thumb-shape-typical-update.png"))
```

If you want to inspect the selection before changing anything, keep it in an object and pass it explicitly:

```{r}
targets <- shape_select(x, name = "Image placeholder marker", match = "exact")
targets[, c("slide_idx", "name", "text", "kind")]

x <- shape_update(x, targets, text = "Ready")
```

## What Works Now

The current implementation covers top-level shape selection and focused updates of selected shapes. It is designed for simple, predictable template markers rather than arbitrary PowerPoint editing.

Supported now:

- Select top-level slide objects such as shapes, text boxes, pictures, connectors, tables, charts, and groups.
- Search one slide, several slides, or all slides.
- Match by visible text and Selection Pane name.
- Filter by XML ID, object kind, placeholder status, placeholder type, and hidden state.
- Return geometry in slide-level inches.
- Add regular non-placeholder shapes with `shape_add()`.
- Modify selected shapes with `shape_update()`.
- Update ordinary non-placeholder shapes; placeholder status is metadata, not a prerequisite.

Not supported yet:

- Recursively selecting shapes inside groups.
- Removing shapes or replacing pictures.
- Detailed run-level text formatting.
- Treating XML IDs as persistent identifiers.
- Resolving layout placeholders such as `ph_location_label()`; use officer's placeholder functions for that.

## Matching

The `match` argument controls how `text` and `name` filters are interpreted.

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `"contains"` | Default. Fixed substring matching. |
| `"exact"` | Complete-value matching after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. |
| `"regex"` | Regular-expression matching. |

### Contains Matching

`contains` is the default because marker text is often embedded in helper text while designing templates. The example template has three marker shapes, so a partial marker such as `{tag_` finds all of them.

```{r}
x <- read_pptx(shape_example_pptx())

shape_select(x, text = "{tag_")[, c("slide_idx", "name", "text")]
```

### Exact Matching

Use `match = "exact"` when the whole shape text should be the marker. Leading and trailing whitespace are ignored.

```{r}
shape_select(x, text = "{tag_1}", match = "exact")[, c("slide_idx", "name", "text")]
```

### Regex Matching

Use `match = "regex"` for marker families.

```{r}
shape_select(
  x,
  text = "^\\s*\\{tag_[0-9]+\\}\\s*$",
  match = "regex"
)[, c("slide_idx", "name", "text")]
```

## Filtering by Metadata

Different criteria are combined with AND. Multiple values within one criterion are alternatives.

```{r}
shape_select(
  x,
  text = "{tag_",
  name = "Rechteck"
)[, c("slide_idx", "shape_idx", "name", "text", "kind")]
```

Object kinds currently include:

| Kind | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `"shape"` | Regular PowerPoint shape or text box. |
| `"picture"` | Picture object. |
| `"table"` | Table graphic frame. |
| `"chart"` | Chart graphic frame. |
| `"graphic_frame"` | Other graphic frame. |
| `"group"` | Top-level group. |
| `"connector"` | Connector shape. |

## Result Columns

`shape_select()` returns a tibble-like `pptx_shape_selection` object. For most workflows, the most useful columns are `slide_idx`, `name`, `text`, `kind`, and the frame columns `left`, `top`, `width`, and `height`.

The `node` list-column is kept in the object for downstream functions, but hidden by the print method.

Important columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `slide_idx` | Visible presentation slide index. |
| `shape_idx` | Top-level shape-tree position, which approximates z-order. |
| `id` | Current slide-local XML shape ID. Not stable across save operations. |
| `name` | Selection Pane name. |
| `text` | Visible text. For groups this is `NA` in the first implementation. |
| `kind` | Object kind. |
| `placeholder` | Whether the object is an actual placeholder. |
| `ph_type` | Placeholder type, if present. |
| `hidden` | Whether `p:cNvPr/@hidden` is set to `"1"`. |
| `left`, `top`, `width`, `height` | Slide-level frame in inches. |
| `rotation` | Rotation in degrees, if present. |
| `description` | Alternative text description, if present. |
| `node` | XML node reference for downstream code. |

```{r}
targets <- shape_select(x, text = "{tag_")
names(targets)
```

Selections also carry internal source metadata. Functions such as `shape_update()` use it to reject selections from a different presentation or selections that became stale after saving, reparsing, deleting shapes, or changing slide order. If that happens, rerun `shape_select()`.

## Adding Shapes

Use `shape_add()` to create ordinary non-placeholder shapes from coordinates. The function creates top-level regular PowerPoint shapes, appends them frontmost, and returns the modified `rpptx` object.

Here, a new rounded rectangle is inserted in the open space between the two upper markers and the lower marker. It uses the same left edge and width as the lower marker, so it aligns with the template structure.

```{r}
x <- shape_add(
  x,
  left = 0.826,
  top = 2.25,
  width = 8.19,
  height = 0.8,
  text = "New shape",
  geometry = "roundRect",
  background = "#E6F4EA",
  line = sp_line(color = "#408335", lwd = 1.5),
  name = "Added shape"
)

shape_select(x, name = "Added shape", match = "exact")[
  , c("name", "text", "placeholder", "left", "top", "width", "height")
]
```

The shape is created with `<p:nvPr/>` and without `<p:ph/>`, so it is not treated as a layout placeholder.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "70%"

knitr::include_graphics(shape_thumbnail("thumb-shape-add.png"))
```

## Update Options

Use `shape_update()` when a selected marker should be changed in place. The function returns the modified `rpptx` object. You can either pass the selection explicitly or pipe the selection directly into `shape_update()`.

```{r}
targets <- shape_select(x, text = "{tag_2}", match = "exact")

x <- shape_update(
  x,
  targets,
  text = "Delayed",
  background = "#FCE8E6",
  line = sp_line(color = "#EC0016", lwd = 1.5),
  name = "Status marker",
  description = "Current service status",
  hidden = FALSE
)

shape_select(x, name = "Status marker", match = "exact")[
  , c("name", "text", "description", "hidden")
]
```

The direct pipe form keeps shape updates inside the presentation pipeline:

```{r}
x <- x |>
  shape_select(name = "Status marker", match = "exact") |>
  shape_update(text = "On time")
```

`shape_update()` edits existing XML nodes. It does not remove and recreate shapes, so z-order and shape identity are preserved.

Supported update arguments:

| Argument | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `text` | Replace the complete visible text. |
| `background` | Set a solid fill. Use `"transparent"` for no fill. |
| `line` | Apply an `officer::sp_line()` outline. |
| `left`, `top`, `width`, `height` | Update position and size in inches. |
| `rotation` | Update rotation in degrees. |
| `name` | Update the Selection Pane name. |
| `description` | Update alt text description. Use `NA` to remove it. |
| `hidden` | Hide or show the shape. |

Different shape kinds have different capabilities. Regular shapes support all update arguments. Connectors support line, geometry, metadata, and visibility. Pictures support line, geometry, metadata, and visibility. Graphic frames and groups currently support geometry, metadata, and visibility.

### Updating Multiple Shapes

Both `shape_add()` and `shape_update()` work row-wise. Scalar values are recycled to all shapes. Vectors and lists with the same length as the selection are applied row by row.

The following example starts again from `shapes.pptx`, selects all three marker shapes, and updates their text, fill, outline, and alt-text descriptions in one call.

```{r}
template <- read_pptx(shape_example_pptx())
targets <- shape_select(template, text = "{tag_", match = "contains")
status <- c(
  "{tag_1}" = "On time",
  "{tag_2}" = "Delayed",
  "{tag_3}" = "Cancelled"
)
background <- c(
  "{tag_1}" = "#E6F4EA",
  "{tag_2}" = "#FFF4CE",
  "{tag_3}" = "#FCE8E6"
)
line <- list(
  "{tag_1}" = sp_line(color = "#408335", lwd = 1.5),
  "{tag_2}" = sp_line(color = "#F39200", lwd = 1.5),
  "{tag_3}" = sp_line(color = "#EC0016", lwd = 1.5)
)
description <- c(
  "{tag_1}" = "Green status marker",
  "{tag_2}" = "Yellow status marker",
  "{tag_3}" = "Red status marker"
)

updated <- shape_update(
  template,
  targets,
  text = unname(status[targets$text]),
  background = unname(background[targets$text]),
  line = unname(line[targets$text]),
  description = unname(description[targets$text]),
  name = paste("Status marker", seq_len(nrow(targets)))
)

shape_select(updated, name = "Status marker", match = "contains")[
  , c("name", "text", "description")
]
```

The thumbnails show the marker slide before and after the update:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "49%"
#| fig-show: hold

knitr::include_graphics(shape_thumbnail(c(
  "thumb-shape-update-before.png",
  "thumb-shape-update-after.png"
)))
```

The demo markers are created with `shape_add()`, so they are ordinary non-placeholder shapes. `shape_update()` updates those selected slide XML nodes in place. The test suite also covers ordinary non-placeholder shapes with `<p:nvPr/>` and no `<p:ph/>`.

## Groups

The first implementation is top-level only. A group is returned as one row with `kind = "group"`; shapes inside the group are not listed or matched.

This keeps coordinates simple and reliable. Recursive group support would need separate handling for group-relative coordinates, nested z-order, rotation, and possible duplicate matches between a group and its children.

## Relation to officer Placeholders

`shape_select()` works on actual slide XML nodes. It is different from officer's `ph_location_*()` functions, which resolve layout placeholders.

Use `ph_location_*()` when you are creating new content from a layout. Use `shape_select()` when an existing slide already contains marker shapes that should be discovered.

`shape_update()` follows the same rule. It updates selected slide XML nodes and does not require those nodes to be placeholders. Ordinary PowerPoint shapes with `<p:nvPr/>` and no `<p:ph/>` are supported and covered by tests.

## Future Extensions

`image_insert()` is the first function built on shape selection to add new
content at marker positions. It selects shapes by text or via `shape_select()`,
then inserts fitted images directly above the targets. See
`vignette("image-insert")` for the full workflow.

```{r}
#| eval: false
targets <- shape_select(template, text = "{photo}")
template <- image_insert(template, image = "photo.png", selection = targets)
template <- shape_update(template, targets, hidden = TRUE)
```

Future functions can extend the same architecture to format text runs, reorder
shapes, or edit shapes inside groups.
